entries.appliesTo: licensed mental-health professionals/providers, and any individual, corporation, or entity offering therapy or psychotherapy services in Rhode Island

dutySources.disclosure-ui: § 40.1-5.5-3(a)(1) — 'is informed in writing of the following' ... '(1) That artificial intelligence will be used'
dutySources.consent-workflow: § 40.1-5.5-3(a) — 'is informed in writing of the following and provides consent as defined'
dutySources.human-review: § 40.1-5.5-3(c)(1) — 'may not allow or otherwise use artificial intelligence to do any of the following' ... 'Make independent therapeutic decisions'

sources.aiTherapyRule: § 40.1-5.5-3(b)–(c) — '(b) An individual, corporation, or entity may not provide, advertise, or otherwise offer' therapy including via AI unless 'conducted' 'by an individual who is a licensed professional or provider'; '(c) A licensed professional or provider may use artificial intelligence only to the extent that' it 'meets the requirements of subsection (a)'
sources.consentRequired: § 40.1-5.5-3(a) — 'is informed in writing of the following and provides consent as defined'
sources.scope: § 40.1-5.5-2(10) — '"Therapy or psychotherapy services" means services provided to diagnose or treat an' 'individual's mental health or behavioral health'
sources.enforcer: § 40.1-5.5-5(a)–(b) — '(a) The penalties pursuant to § 5-37.3-9 shall apply to any violation of the confidentiality' 'provisions of this chapter'; '(b) The executive office of health and human services shall have authority to investigate'

flags: aiTherapyRule 'supervised' is lossy: standalone/unlicensed AI therapy is prohibited outright (§ 40.1-5.5-3(b)) while licensed providers may use AI for administrative/supplementary support under consent and oversight (§ 40.1-5.5-3(a),(c))

consent/disclosure trigger in § 40.1-5.5-3(a) is narrowed to AI 'designed to simulate emotional attachment, bonding, or dependency or artificial intelligence companions' used 'where the client's therapeutic session is recorded or transcribed'
confidentiality duty (§ 40.1-5.5-4 — records and communications 'shall be confidential and shall not be disclosed except as provided pursuant to the provisions of § 40.1-') fits no listed duty key
penalties are cross-referenced (§ 5-37.3-9) and apply only to 'the confidentiality provisions of this chapter'; no penalty stated for other violations, so no penaltyMax coded
exemptions in § 40.1-5.5-5(c): religious counseling, peer support, public self-help/educational materials, FDA-cleared (or other federal-agency-approved) AI tools, and IRB-approved research
§ 40.1-5.5-6 authorizes EOHHS rulemaking to carry out the chapter
